context:
Do not introduce a custom forked build of duckdb-wasm unless every
other avenue fails. Prefer a library upgrade, then a supported config
entry point, then an upstream fix. The goal is to keep the explorer's
HTTP attach logic conventional so future maintainers do not carry a
private patch.
description:
The explorer attaches `results.duckdb` at
`results-explorer/src/db.ts` via
`registerFileURL("results.duckdb", url, DuckDBDataProtocol.HTTP, true)`
followed by `ATTACH 'results.duckdb' AS bench (READ_ONLY)`. The RG-2
gate for the canonical browser read model requires that a cold
single-row lookup transfers ≤10% of the on-disk DB, i.e. DuckDB-WASM
should use HTTP `Range:` requests rather than a single whole-file GET.

In practice, with duckdb-wasm 1.32.0, the runtime's HTTP file-info
defaults (`reliableHeadRequests=false`, `allowFullHttpReads=true`)
short-circuit the Range probe even when `directIO=true` is passed to
`registerFileURL`, and the runtime falls back to a single whole-file
GET on ATTACH. There is no stable per-URL API to override those
defaults from the main thread:

- `db.open({filesystem: {reliableHeadRequests: true, allowFullHTTPReads: false}})`
  resets the WebFileSystem and breaks the already-registered URL.
- `SET reliable_head_requests = true` affects only the httpfs extension
  HTTP client, not the runtime's built-in HTTP file reader.
- The per-file `_globalFileInfo` object that carries these flags lives
  inside the DuckDB-WASM worker and is not reachable from the page.

The e2e harness already serves the snapshot with `Accept-Ranges: bytes`
and honours `Range: bytes=...` with `206 Partial Content` (see
`results-explorer/scripts/serve-browser-tests.mjs` and
`results-explorer/e2e/capability/range-read-budget.spec.ts`), so the
moment the browser runtime starts issuing range reads, the RG-2
byte-budget assertion can be re-introduced without any server change.

Deliverables:
1. Confirm the library-level behaviour against the current
   duckdb-wasm version at the time of work start (it may have
   gained a supported override by then).
2. Pick a path from: (a) upgrade duckdb-wasm to a version that
   supports per-URL range-read flags, (b) patch the runtime via a
   supported entry point such as a config object accepted by
   `registerFileURL`, or (c) file an upstream issue/PR and pin to a
   build that includes the fix.
3. Re-enable the byte-budget assertion in
   `results-explorer/e2e/capability/range-read-budget.spec.ts` using
   the server-side `/__test/transfers` accounting already in place.

anti_patterns.instead: solve the problem via a supported configuration surface instead.
anti_patterns.why: it lives inside the DuckDB-WASM worker and crosses a private API boundary

anti_patterns.dont: move the explorer off DuckDB-WASM's HTTP attach to regain range reads
anti_patterns.instead: fix the range-read path rather than replacing it.
anti_patterns.why: the canonical browser read model depends on it

preserves.behavior: The server-side transfer log at `/__test/transfers` remains available for the re-enabled assertion.
The test server's `Accept-Ranges`/`Range` handling in `results-explorer/scripts/serve-browser-tests.mjs` is not regressed.
`results-explorer/src/db.ts` continues to ATTACH the snapshot READ_ONLY and must not fall back to a JSON-only path.

verifications.description: The TODO item itself validates cleanly
verifications.expected: Validation passes with no schema or DAG errors

verifications.command: cd results-explorer && npm run test:e2e:chromium -- --grep "RG-2 range-read"
verifications.description: After the fix lands, a cold explorer load transfers ≤10% of the snapshot
verifications.expected: The byte-budget assertion is re-enabled and passes

work_units.notes:
Audited duckdb-wasm 1.32.0 (latest stable as of 2026-04-27;
1.33.x exists only as dev pre-release builds). Findings:

- `DuckDBConfig.filesystem` in
  `dist/types/src/bindings/config.d.ts` exposes three booleans:
  `reliableHeadRequests`, `allowFullHTTPReads`, and
  `forceFullHTTPReads`. There is no per-URL override on
  `registerFileURL`.
- `db.open({filesystem: {...}})` is the public entry point.
- Order matters: `open` AFTER `registerFileURL` resets the
  WebFileSystem and breaks the registration; `open` BEFORE
  registration is the supported sequence.
- `allowFullHTTPReads: false` makes the runtime error on
  first ATTACH ("IO Error: Cannot open database 'results.duckdb'
  in read-only mode: database does not exist"). This matches
  upstream issue duckdb/duckdb-wasm#1984's analysis: when the
  flag is false the runtime "always errors". So we cannot use it
  to force range-only reads.
- With `reliableHeadRequests: true` + `forceFullHTTPReads: false`
  + the default `allowFullHTTPReads: true`, the page loads but
  the runtime still issues a single whole-file GET against the
  registered URL (verified by the test harness transfer log:
  total 6,565,888 bytes = full DB size, no 206 responses).
- Issue #1984 documents the underlying buggy code path: even
  when the runtime first attempts a range read, an extra "full
  GET anyway" code block runs after. This block has not been
  removed in 1.32.0.

Conclusion: there is no flag combination on duckdb-wasm 1.32.0
that yields range-only reads against an HTTP-registered URL.
The fix must come from upstream (or from a 1.33.x stable
release once one ships). The byte-budget assertion has been
added to range-read-budget.spec.ts under `test.skip` so it
auto-enables when the runtime starts issuing 206s.

Update 2026-04-27: also verified against `@duckdb/duckdb-wasm@
1.33.1-dev53.0` (the latest dev pre-release). Same behavior —
whole-file GET on ATTACH, zero 206 responses, byte-budget
exceeded by 10x. Upstream has not addressed this in any 1.33.x
build to date. Reverted to 1.32.0.
work_units.summary: Re-audit duckdb-wasm runtime flags and the HTTP file-reader code path for the current version

work_units.notes:
Update 2026-05-01: still blocked on upstream. Current npm metadata
shows no stable `@duckdb/duckdb-wasm` release beyond `1.32.0`; the
package dist-tags point at dev builds (`latest=1.33.1-dev45.0`,
`next=1.33.1-dev53.0`). Upstream issue duckdb/duckdb-wasm#1984 is
still open, with no maintainer resolution or release note indicating
a supported range-only path for HTTP-registered URLs.

`/code review W2`: no required code changes are available under the
TODO guardrails. Upgrading to a dev pre-release or carrying a private
patched runtime would violate the `approach` constraint unless the
maintainer explicitly accepts that tradeoff.

Of the three candidate paths:

1. **Library upgrade** — no stable 1.33.x release is available
   (only dev builds 1.33.1-dev1 through 1.33.1-dev53 as of
   2026-05-01). Pinning to a dev pre-release violates the
   `approach` constraint ("Do not introduce a custom forked build
   of duckdb-wasm unless every other avenue fails").
2. **Supported runtime API** — w1 verified that no flag
   combination on the public `DuckDBConfig.filesystem` API yields
   range-only reads. The buggy "Perform a full GET anyways" code
   path in runtime_browser.ts is not toggleable from the page.
3. **Upstream issue/PR** — this is the path forward. File or
   comment on duckdb/duckdb-wasm#1984 with a minimal repro
   showing that even `reliableHeadRequests: true` +
   `forceFullHTTPReads: false` produces a whole-file GET on
   ATTACH against an `HTTP, directIO=true` registration. Pin to
   the first 1.33.x stable that includes the fix.

This work unit unblocks once a 1.33.x stable release with the
fix is published OR a private patched build is acceptable.
work_units.summary: Pick an unblock path and prototype it

work_units.notes:
Partially landed: the byte-budget assertion is now coded in
`results-explorer/e2e/capability/range-read-budget.spec.ts`
under `test.skip`. It asserts after a cold `goto` of `/results/`
followed by `waitForDataLoaded` that:
  - the sum of `Content-Length` transfers under
    `/results/data/results.duckdb` is ≤10% of the on-disk DB
    size, and
  - at least one transfer is a 206 ranged response.

The test is currently `.skip` because w2 is blocked. Removing
`.skip` is a one-line change once the runtime issues range
reads. The capability tests survive as a diagnostic.
work_units.summary: Re-enable the byte-budget assertion and close the RG-2 gate
